create.name: Michael W. Taft
create.bio:
Michael W. Taft has meditated for more than thirty-five years, practising in Zen temples in Japan and in retreat in India, with long experience of Buddhist and Hindu tantric practice. He now teaches a nondual style of meditation in plain, non-religious language. His teaching is organised around a map he calls the Stack Model, which moves from careful vipassana investigation of each sense towards resting as open awareness. Before teaching full time he worked in publishing, including many years as editorial director at Sounds True, and he has also taught classes at Vassar College.

He co-founded the Alembic, a community centre in Berkeley, California, where he leads an evening meditation and talk most Thursdays that is also streamed and archived on his YouTube channel. He hosts the long-form Deconstructing Yourself podcast, runs cohort-based online courses such as Hacking the Stack and Vast Sky Mind, offers one-to-one meditation coaching, and leads residential retreats at Mount Madonna Center near Santa Cruz. His books include The Mindful Geek, a guide to meditation for sceptics, and Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept. His home is in the San Francisco Bay Area, where he lives with his family.

books.title: Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept
books.author: Michael W. Taft
books.description: A short survey of how the idea of nonduality has been described across cultures, from the Upanishads through Buddhism and Advaita Vedanta to present-day Western teachers.

books.title: Ego: The Fall of the Twin Towers and the Rise of an Enlightened Humanity
books.author: Peter Baumann and Michael W. Taft
books.description: Co-written with Peter Baumann, this book traces the human sense of self back through evolution and asks whether people can grow beyond the ego's grip. It draws on neuroscience, psychology and evolutionary biology.

courses.title: Deconstructing Yourself Winter Retreat 2026
courses.description: An eight-day residential nondual meditation retreat at Mount Madonna Center in the hills above Monterey Bay. Room and meals are booked and paid separately with the centre, and scholarship places are offered.
courses.price: $1100 registration plus Mount Madonna room and meals (e.g. $2557 total for a shared room)

courses.title: Online Courses: Hacking the Stack and Vast Sky Mind
courses.description: Twelve-week cohort courses with readings, videos, practice pods and live sessions. Hacking the Stack teaches the foundations of vipassana through his Stack Model; Vast Sky Mind turns to nondual and effortless practice.

courses.title: 1:1 Coaching with Michael Taft
courses.description: Weekly one-to-one meditation sessions by video or phone, usually over about three months, with a practice plan built around the student and time for questions.

free_resources.title: Guided Meditations
free_resources.description: His collection of free recorded guided meditations, including the weekly sessions from the Alembic and earlier series.

free_resources.title: Guided Sleep Meditation – Relaxation
free_resources.description: A free guided relaxation for winding down at night, moving attention slowly through the body.

free_resources.title: What Is Nonduality?
free_resources.description: A free introductory primer on what nonduality means and how it shows up in meditation practice.

free_resources.title: Deconstructing Yourself Podcast
free_resources.description: Long-form conversations he hosts with meditation teachers, researchers and practitioners about awakening and practice.
